passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Make two trumpets of hammered silver to be used for calling the congregation and for having the camps set out.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to make two trumpets.
Moses must use silver to make the trumpets.
Moses must hammer the silver to shape the trumpets.
The trumpets will belong to Moses.
Moses will use the trumpets to call the congregation together.
Moses will also use the trumpets to signal the camps to set out.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ עֲשֵׂ֣ה לְךָ֗ שְׁתֵּי֙ חֲצֽוֹצְרֹ֣ת כֶּ֔סֶף מִקְשָׁ֖ה תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑ם וְהָי֤וּ לְךָ֙ לְמִקְרָ֣א הָֽעֵדָ֔ה וּלְמַסַּ֖ע אֶת־ הַֽמַּחֲנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: When both are sounded, the whole congregation is to assemble before you at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God told Moses to make two silver trumpets.
The trumpets are for calling the people together.
When you sound both trumpets, all the people must gather.
They must come to you.
They must meet at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.original: וְתָקְע֖וּ בָּהֵ֑ן וְנֽוֹעֲד֤וּ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה אֶל־ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: But if only one is sounded, then the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, are to gather before you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses instructions for the people of Israel.
God told Moses to make two silver trumpets.
The trumpets are for calling the people and for signaling the camps to move.
If you sound only one trumpet,
the leaders must come to you.
These leaders are the heads of the clans of Israel.
They will gather before you.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בְּאַחַ֖ת יִתְקָ֑עוּ וְנוֹעֲד֤וּ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ הַנְּשִׂיאִ֔ים רָאשֵׁ֖י אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: When you sound short blasts, the camps that lie on the east side are to set out.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites camped in the wilderness.
Some camps stayed on the east side.
You must sound short blasts on the trumpets.
When you sound the short blasts, the camps on the east side must set out.
passages.original: וּתְקַעְתֶּ֖ם תְּרוּעָ֑ה וְנָֽסְעוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנ֔וֹת הַחֹנִ֖ים קֵֽדְמָה׃

passages.text: When you sound the short blasts a second time, the camps that lie on the south side are to set out. The blasts are to signal them to set out.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites camped in the wilderness.
The priests are the sons of Aaron.
The priests sound the trumpets.
You must sound short blasts on the trumpets a second time.
The camps on the south side must set out when they hear the second short blasts.
The short blasts signal the camps on the south side to begin their journey.
passages.original: וּתְקַעְתֶּ֤ם תְּרוּעָה֙ שֵׁנִ֔ית וְנָֽסְעוּ֙ הַֽמַּחֲנ֔וֹת הַחֹנִ֖ים תֵּימָ֑נָה תְּרוּעָ֥ה יִתְקְע֖וּ לְמַסְעֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: To convene the assembly, you are to sound long blasts, not short ones.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites must gather the assembly at times.
They must sound the trumpets to call the people together.
They must use long blasts on the trumpets.
They must not use short blasts.
passages.original: וּבְהַקְהִ֖יל אֶת־ הַקָּהָ֑ל תִּתְקְע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א תָרִֽיעוּ׃

passages.text: The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to sound the trumpets. This shall be a permanent statute for you and the generations to come.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Aaron are priests.
The priests must sound the trumpets.
God commands this rule.
This rule will last forever.
This rule is for you and your descendants.
passages.original: וּבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים יִתְקְע֖וּ בַּֽחֲצֹצְר֑וֹת וְהָי֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם לְחֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: When you enter into battle in your land against an adversary who attacks you, sound short blasts on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites live in their own land.
Sometimes, enemies attack the Israelites in their land.
When this happens, the Israelites must go to battle.
The Israelites must sound short blasts on the trumpets.
The sons of Aaron, who are priests, must blow the trumpets.
God will remember the Israelites when they sound the trumpets.
God is the LORD, their God.
God will save the Israelites from their enemies.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ תָבֹ֨אוּ מִלְחָמָ֜ה בְּאַרְצְכֶ֗ם עַל־ הַצַּר֙ הַצֹּרֵ֣ר אֶתְכֶ֔ם וַהֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם בַּחֲצֹצְר֑וֹת וֲנִזְכַּרְתֶּ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וְנוֹשַׁעְתֶּ֖ם מֵאֹיְבֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And on your joyous occasions, your appointed feasts, and the beginning of each month, you are to blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to serve as a reminder for you before your God. I am the LORD your God.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
He commands you to remember Him.
On your days of joy, blow the trumpets.
On your appointed feasts, blow the trumpets.
At the beginning of each month, blow the trumpets.
Blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings.
Blow the trumpets over your fellowship offerings.
These trumpet blasts will remind you before your God.
passages.original: וּבְי֨וֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶ֥ם וּֽבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֮ וּבְרָאשֵׁ֣י חָדְשֵׁיכֶם֒ וּתְקַעְתֶּ֣ם בַּחֲצֹֽצְרֹ֗ת עַ֚ל עֹלֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעַ֖ל זִבְחֵ֣י שַׁלְמֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָי֨וּ לָכֶ֤ם לְזִכָּרוֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle of the Testimony, and the Israelites set out from the Wilderness of Sinai, traveling from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were in the wilderness.
They had built the tabernacle of the Testimony.
This tabernacle was a special tent for God’s presence.
A cloud stayed above the tabernacle.
The cloud showed that God was with them.
It was the second year after they left Egypt.
It was the second month.
It was the twentieth day of the month.
On that day, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle.
The Israelites saw the cloud move.
They left the Wilderness of Sinai.
They began their journey.
They traveled from place to place.
They followed the cloud.
The cloud stopped in the Wilderness of Paran.
The Israelites camped there.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֧ה הַשֵּׁנִ֛ית בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֖י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים בַּחֹ֑דֶשׁ נַעֲלָה֙ הֶֽעָנָ֔ן מֵעַ֖ל מִשְׁכַּ֥ן הָעֵדֻֽת׃ וַיִּסְע֧וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְמַסְעֵיהֶ֖ם מִמִּדְבַּ֣ר סִינָ֑י וַיִּשְׁכֹּ֥ן הֶעָנָ֖ן בְּמִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָֽן׃

passages.text: They set out this first time according to the LORD’s command through Moses.
passages.sermon: The Israelites set out for the first time.\r\nThey obeyed the LORD’s command.\r\nMoses gave them the LORD’s instruction.
passages.original: וַיִּסְע֖וּ בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה עַל־ פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃

passages.text: First, the divisions of the camp of Judah set out under their standard, with Nahshon son of Amminadab in command.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Judah was one of the tribes of Israel.
The Israelites were traveling in the wilderness.
The camp of Judah had its own divisions.
The divisions of the camp of Judah set out first.
They marched under their own standard.
Nahshon was the leader of the camp of Judah.
Nahshon was the son of Amminadab.
passages.original: וַיִּסַּ֞ע דֶּ֣גֶל מַחֲנֵ֧ה בְנֵֽי־ יְהוּדָ֛ה בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֖ה לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְעַל־ צְבָא֔וֹ נַחְשׁ֖וֹן בֶּן־ עַמִּינָדָֽב׃

passages.text: Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar, and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
passages.sermon:
Nethanel was the son of Zuar.
He led the division of the tribe of Issachar.
Eliab was the son of Helon.
He led the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
passages.original: וְעַ֨ל־ צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י יִשָׂשכָ֑ר נְתַנְאֵ֖ל בֶּן־ צוּעָֽר׃ וְעַ֨ל־ צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י זְבוּלֻ֑ן אֱלִיאָ֖ב בֶּן־ חֵלֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites set out, transporting it.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites had a tabernacle.
The tabernacle was a holy tent.
The people took down the tabernacle.
The Gershonites were a group from the tribe of Levi.
The Merarites were also a group from the tribe of Levi.
The Gershonites and the Merarites carried the tabernacle.
The Gershonites and the Merarites set out on the journey.
They transported the tabernacle.
passages.original: וְהוּרַ֖ד הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן וְנָסְע֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ גֵרְשׁוֹן֙ וּבְנֵ֣י מְרָרִ֔י נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃ס

passages.text: Then the divisions of the camp of Reuben set out under their standard, with Elizur son of Shedeur in command.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Reuben had a camp.
\r\nThis camp had divisions.
\r\nThe divisions of the camp of Reuben set out.
\r\nThey marched under their own standard.
\r\nElizur was the leader of these divisions.
\r\nElizur was the son of Shedeur.
passages.original: וְנָסַ֗ע דֶּ֛גֶל מַחֲנֵ֥ה רְאוּבֵ֖ן לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְעַל־ צְבָא֔וֹ אֱלִיצ֖וּר בֶּן־ שְׁדֵיאֽוּר׃

passages.text: Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon, and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.
passages.sermon:
Shelumiel was the son of Zurishaddai.
Shelumiel led the division of the tribe of Simeon.
Eliasaph was the son of Deuel.
Eliasaph led the division of the tribe of Gad.
passages.original: וְעַ֨ל־ צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֑וֹן שְׁלֻֽמִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־ צוּרִֽי שַׁדָּֽי׃ וְעַל־ צְבָ֖א מַטֵּ֣ה בְנֵי־ גָ֑ד אֶלְיָסָ֖ף בֶּן־ דְּעוּאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Then the Kohathites set out, transporting the holy objects; the tabernacle was to be set up before their arrival.
passages.sermon:
The Kohathites were Levites.
The Kohathites carried the holy objects.
The Kohathites set out on their journey.
Others set up the tabernacle before the Kohathites arrived.
passages.original: וְנָסְעוּ֙ הַקְּהָתִ֔ים נֹשְׂאֵ֖י הַמִּקְדָּ֑שׁ וְהֵקִ֥ימוּ אֶת־ הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן עַד־ בֹּאָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Next, the divisions of the camp of Ephraim set out under their standard, with Elishama son of Ammihud in command.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Ephraim had its own camp.
This camp had several divisions.
Each division belonged to the tribe of Ephraim.
The people of Ephraim marched together.
They marched under their own banner.
Elishama was the leader of this camp.
Elishama was the son of Ammihud.
Elishama commanded the divisions of Ephraim.
passages.original: וְנָסַ֗ע דֶּ֛גֶל מַחֲנֵ֥ה בְנֵֽי־ אֶפְרַ֖יִם לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְעַל־ צְבָא֔וֹ אֱלִישָׁמָ֖ע בֶּן־ עַמִּיהֽוּד׃

passages.text: Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh, and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
passages.sermon:
Gamaliel was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh.
Gamaliel was the son of Pedahzur.
Abidan was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin.
Abidan was the son of Gideoni.
passages.original: וְעַ֨ל־ צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה גַּמְלִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־ פְּדָה־ צֽוּר׃ וְעַ֨ל־ צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן אֲבִידָ֖ן בֶּן־ גִּדְעוֹנִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Finally, the divisions of the camp of Dan set out under their standard, serving as the rear guard for all units, with Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai in command.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Dan had a camp.
The camp of Dan had its own divisions.
The people of Dan marched last.
They served as the rear guard for all the camps of Israel.
They marched under their own standard.
Ahiezer was their leader.
Ahiezer was the son of Ammishaddai.
passages.original: וְנָסַ֗ע דֶּ֚גֶל מַחֲנֵ֣ה בְנֵי־ דָ֔ן מְאַסֵּ֥ף לְכָל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֹ֖ת לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וְעַל־ צְבָא֔וֹ אֲחִיעֶ֖זֶר בֶּן־ עַמִּישַׁדָּֽי׃

passages.text: Pagiel son of Ocran was over the division of the tribe of Asher, and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
passages.sermon:
Pagiel was the leader of the tribe of Asher.
Pagiel was the son of Ocran.
Ahira was the leader of the tribe of Naphtali.
Ahira was the son of Enan.
passages.original: וְעַל־ צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י אָשֵׁ֑ר פַּגְעִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־ עָכְרָֽן׃ וְעַ֨ל־ צְבָ֔א מַטֵּ֖ה בְּנֵ֣י נַפְתָּלִ֑י אֲחִירַ֖ע בֶּן־ עֵינָֽן׃

passages.text: This was the order of march for the Israelite divisions as they set out.
passages.sermon: The Israelites traveled in groups called divisions.\r\nEach division had its own order for marching.\r\nThe Israelites set out according to this order.
passages.original: אֵ֛לֶּה מַסְעֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְצִבְאֹתָ֑ם וַיִּסָּֽעוּ׃ס

passages.text: Then Moses said to Hobab, the son of Moses’ father-in-law Reuel the Midianite, “We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said: ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Hobab.
Hobab was the son of Reuel the Midianite.
Reuel was Moses’ father-in-law.
Moses said, “We are setting out for a place.”
The LORD said about this place, ‘I will give it to you.’
Moses said, “Come with us.”
Moses said, “We will treat you well.”
The LORD has promised good things to Israel.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֗ה לְ֠חֹבָב בֶּן־ רְעוּאֵ֣ל הַמִּדְיָנִי֮ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁה֒ נֹסְעִ֣ים׀ אֲנַ֗חְנוּ אֶל־ הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֹת֖וֹ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָכֶ֑ם לְכָ֤ה אִתָּ֙נוּ֙ וְהֵטַ֣בְנוּ לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־ יְהוָ֥ה דִּבֶּר־ ט֖וֹב עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “I will not go,” Hobab replied. “Instead, I am going back to my own land and my own people.”
passages.sermon:
Hobab was the son of Reuel the Midianite.  
Reuel was Moses’ father-in-law.  
Moses invited Hobab to travel with the Israelites.  
Hobab answered Moses.  
Hobab said, “I will not go.”  
Hobab said, “I will return to my own land.”  
Hobab said, “I will return to my own people.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו לֹ֣א אֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּ֧י אִם־ אֶל־ אַרְצִ֛י וְאֶל־ מוֹלַדְתִּ֖י אֵלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: “Please do not leave us,” Moses said, “since you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can serve as our eyes.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Hobab.
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Hobab was the son of Reuel the Midianite.
Reuel was Moses’ father-in-law.
Moses said, “Please do not leave us.”
Moses said, “You know where we should camp in the wilderness.”
Moses said, “You can serve as our eyes.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַל־ נָ֖א תַּעֲזֹ֣ב אֹתָ֑נוּ כִּ֣י׀ עַל־ כֵּ֣ן יָדַ֗עְתָּ חֲנֹתֵ֙נוּ֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְהָיִ֥יתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְעֵינָֽיִם׃

passages.text: If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Hobab.
Moses asked Hobab to come with the Israelites.
Moses said, “If you come with us, the LORD will do good things for us.
We will do good to you.
We will share with you whatever good things the LORD gives us.”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֖ה כִּי־ תֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֑נוּ וְהָיָ֣ה׀ הַטּ֣וֹב הַה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵיטִ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה עִמָּ֖נוּ וְהֵטַ֥בְנוּ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: So they set out on a three-day journey from the mountain of the LORD, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD traveling ahead of them for those three days to seek a resting place for them.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites left the mountain of the LORD.
They began a journey that lasted three days.
The ark of the covenant of the LORD went in front of them.
The ark traveled ahead for those three days.
The ark looked for a place where the people could rest.
passages.original: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵהַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה דֶּ֖רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וַאֲר֨וֹן בְּרִית־ יְהוָ֜ה נֹסֵ֣עַ לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים לָת֥וּר לָהֶ֖ם מְנוּחָֽה׃

passages.text: And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD sent a cloud.
The cloud was over the people.
The cloud was there during the day.
The people set out from the camp.
The cloud covered them as they traveled.
passages.original: וַעֲנַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יוֹמָ֑ם בְּנָסְעָ֖ם מִן־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃׆ס

passages.text: Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You.”
passages.sermon:
Moses led the people of Israel in the wilderness.
The ark of the covenant went ahead of them.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses spoke.
Moses said, "Rise up, O LORD."
He said, "May Your enemies be scattered."
He said, "May those who hate You flee before You."
passages.original: וַיְהִ֛י בִּנְסֹ֥עַ הָאָרֹ֖ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֑ה קוּמָ֣ה׀ יְהוָ֗ה וְיָפֻ֙צוּ֙ אֹֽיְבֶ֔יךָ וְיָנֻ֥סוּ מְשַׂנְאֶ֖יךָ מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: And when it came to rest, he would say: “Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
The Israelites traveled through the wilderness.
They carried the ark of the covenant with them.
When the ark stopped and rested, Moses spoke.
Moses said, “Return, O LORD.”
He asked God to come back to the people of Israel.
He spoke to God about the countless thousands of Israelites.
Moses wanted God’s presence to be with all the people.
passages.original: וּבְנֻחֹ֖ה יֹאמַ֑ר שׁוּבָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה רִֽבְב֖וֹת אַלְפֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃׆ס
